name: Russell's retrospective synthesis of the medieval Catholic worldview
plain_explanation: Russell opens the chapter by summarizing how the whole medieval Christian synthesis was built: Greek philosophy provided the intellectual framework, Eastern 'mystery religion' elements (dying-and-rising gods, sacramental meals, baptism-like second birth, a separated magical priesthood, impressive ritual, and Persian dualism -- good vs. evil, Ahura Mazda vs. Ahriman, with Satan descending from Ahriman) supplied much of Christianity's religious power, and Roman administrative methods gave the Church its organizational strength. He argues Christianity succeeded partly by combining a Jewish-style sacred book and exclusive truth-claim with a more universal (non-racial) appeal, and by offering sharper doctrines of heaven and hell than either the Jews or the pagan mystery cults.
precise_definition: Russell's summary account of medieval Catholicism as a historical synthesis of Greek philosophy, Near Eastern mystery-religion and dualist elements (absorbed into Hellenistic culture after Alexander and channeled through Neoplatonism), Jewish scriptural monotheism, and Roman methods of hierarchical administration.
why_it_mattered: It functions as Russell's closing assessment of everything traced across Book Two, explaining both the sources of the medieval Church's unprecedented strength ('a strength which no earlier social organization had equalled') and, implicitly, the complexity of forces whose fourteenth-century weakening the rest of the chapter narrates.
historical_origin: Presented by Russell as a retrospective synthesis at the opening of the chapter, summarizing material developed across the whole of Book Two and, implicitly, Book One.
examples: The dying and resurrected god and sacramental eating of the god's flesh, absorbed from Near Eastern mystery religion
Persian dualism (Ahura Mazda vs. Ahriman) reworked into Christian teaching, with Satan developed from Ahriman
Easter combining the Jewish Passover with pagan resurrected-god celebrations
connection_to_politics_or_religion: The entire concept is explicitly about the fusion of religion, philosophy, and political administration into a single, historically unprecedented institution.
